plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Bare, gnarled branches break into spicy-sweet blossoms in shades of blush pink and white. The flowers open before any leaves appear. Their perfume drifts through gardens and orchards while winter is still in the air.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-winter to early spring, roughly January through March, with peak bloom in February
plants.location: Japan, where ume groves and shrine gardens are in flower in late February, weeks before cherry blossoms
plants.funFact: Ume blooms about a month ahead of cherry blossoms. In Japanese culture it stands for perseverance, because it flowers while the cold still lingers. Its fruit is pickled into the tangy umeboshi and steeped into plum wine.

plants.name: Eranthis hyemalis
plants.description: This tiny buttercup-family bulb pushes up golden, cup-shaped flowers, each ringed by a green leafy collar. Where it is happy it spreads into glowing yellow carpets on the bare woodland floor. Flowers are open at about the same time as snowdrops.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, from about February into March
plants.location: Woodlands and gardens across temperate Europe, including central Europe where flowering typically begins in early February and runs through March
plants.funFact: Its flowers track the sun, opening wide in bright light and closing in dull or cold weather. That gives early bees one of the first reliable winter meals.

plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs are covered in rose-like blooms, from single cups to formal, many-petalled doubles. The flowers come in white and every shade of pink and red. They light up gardens when little else is flowering.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring, with February often showing the widest variety of blooms
plants.location: Gardens of the southeastern United States, such as the Carolinas, where camellias are in full flower in February
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant, Camellia sinensis. Thousands of cultivars have been bred, and some bear several flower forms on one bush.
